Aarti Sisodiya vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:22128) on 16
May, 2024
[2024:Rj-Jd:22128]
 High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan At
Jodhpur

S.B. Civil Writ Petition No. 10847/2018
Aarti Sisodiya D/o Shri Vikram Singh Sisodiya, Aged About 34
Years, Byecaste Rajpute, 306, Laxmi Nagar, Banswara
(Rajasthan).

----Petitioner
 Versus
1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Secretary, Department Of
 Rural Development And Panchayati Raj, Govt. Of
 Rajasthan, Secretariat, Jaipur (Raj.).
2. Zila Parishad, Banswara (Rajasthan) Through Its Chief
 Executive Officer.

3. Block Development Officer, Panchayat Sammittee,
 Banswara (Rajasthan).
 ----Respondents
 For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Vijay Kumar
 For Respondent(s) : Mr. Lalit Pareek
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Arun Monga
Judgment (Oral) 16/05/2024
1.

entities.text:
Block Development Officer, Panchayat Sammittee,
 Banswara (Rajasthan)
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner, a young widow owing to the untimely death of her husband in a road accident, is before this Court seeking appropriate directions and/or issuance of writ commanding the respondents to accord her appointment on the post of LDC, for which she had competed vide a recruitment drive carried out in year 2013 and was declared successful.

2. Briefly speaking, relevant facts as pleaded in the petition are that after the death of her husband on 24.01.2010, petitioner applied in the Widow category for the post of LDC for which direct [2024:RJ-JD:22128] (2 of 5) [CW-10847/2018] recruitment was carried out pursuant to an advertisement 2013.

She was successful in the selection and was allotted Panchayat Samiti,
Banswara vide an order dated 27.06.2013.
Subsequent thereto, she was posted at Gram Panchayat Lodha and joined her duties on 03.07.2013.

However, as a bolt from the blue, vide an office order dated 08.08.2013 her services were temporarily terminated subject to verification of her Certificate in Computer Diploma (Annex.1) dated 11.01.2013 issued by University of Sikkim.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In fact, this is the second foray of petitioner before this Court as she had earlier approached by way of filing S.B.C.W.P. No.11059/2013, wherein vide an interim order dated 06.09.2013,
respondents were given liberty to terminate her services, only in the event of getting an adverse report qua verification of her Certificate in Computer Diploma.
2.2. Pursuant thereto, petitioner approached the respondents requesting them to allow to rejoin the duty.
She was permitted to join back as is borne out from the joining report dated 09.09.2013 (Annex.6).

Thereafter, as it turned out, the respondents upon receipt of information qua her Diploma Certificate found the same to be adverse and terminated her services on 01.11.2013 without passing any formal orders.
2.3. Simultaneously, an FIR No.4/2014 was also registered against her under Sections 420 and 467 of IPC.

Pursuant to the FIR, thorough investigation was conducted and vide a closure report dated 29.03.2017, it was recommended by the Investigating Officer that the Certificate in Computer Diploma [2024:RJ-JD:22128] (3 of 5) [CW-10847/2018] submitted by the petitioner from Sikkim University was valid.

Said closure/negative report was duly accepted by the competent court of CJM,
Banswara vide order dated 12.12.2015. 2.4.

Fortified with the closure report in the FIR along with copy of the order passed by the CJM, the petitioner approached the respondents and submitted a formal application dated 25.09.2017 requesting them to allow her to rejoin the duties, since she was earlier not allowed to join during pendency of the FIR.
However, no heed was paid to the same.
Hence, the petition.
3. Defence taken in the reply is that the services of the candidates who acquired Certificate of Computer Diploma from Meghalaya/Sikkim/Manipur were temporarily terminated.
The Panchayat Samiti, Banswara was asked to verify the diploma certificates from the concerned University in the meanwhile.
3.1 The reason for not considering the case of the petitioner to rejoin on the post of LDC is not on account of acquittal from the competent court.

The reason is on account of an order dated 04.08.2017 (Annex.R/1), whereby, the candidates who had acquired computer qualification from Eastern Institute for Integrated Learning in Management University, Sikkim were held to be having invalid qualification by the State Government.
Therefore, the petitioner cannot be permitted to rejoin on the post of LDC.
Hence, this petition is liable to be dismissed.
4. In the aforesaid backdrop, I have heard the rival contentions and gone through the case file.

5. The defence taken in the reply of the respondents and as argued inter alia is that the petitioner cannot be given the [2024:RJ-JD:22128] (4 of 5) [CW-10847/2018] advantage of merit in view of the forged qualification Certificate in Computer Diploma. Record shows that the said defense plea taken by the respondents has since been dealt with in the proceedings before a competent criminal court and totally disbelieved and findings have gone in favour of the petitioner.
It was held that there was no forgery but it was an inadvertent mistake of reading the digit '3' as '8', which led to the initial impression of the certificate being forged.
University is otherwise a recognized institution.
6. After the trial, the petitioner has not only been exonerated, but the State has also chosen not to file any appeal against acquittal order qua the said charge of forgery.

entities.text: Aarti Sisodiya vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:22128)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I am thus compelled to therefore accept the outcome of the criminal proceedings and hold that the Certificate in Computer Diploma awarded to the petitioner is genuine and the benefit thereof has to be given to her.

8. As regards the State Government having derecognized the Eastern Institute for Integrated Learning in Management University, Sikkim vide order dated 04.08.2017, the same cannot be given retrospective legal cognizance if the petitioner's services were not terminated by the respondents way back in the year 2013.

entities.text: Eastern Institute for Integrated Learning in Management University, Sikkim
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 9. Needless to say, at that time since the University was recognized by the State Government petitioner would have continued in service.

Any service benefits enured during the time when the degree was valid would have since crystallized and the [2024:RJ-JD:22128] (5 of 5)
[CW-10847/2018] subsequent derecognition could not have been taken away the same from the petitioner.
10. In the premise, I see no reason for not accepting the qualification certificate, which was found to be valid by a competent court after threadbare trial.
11. As an upshot, the petition is allowed.
The impugned temporary rejection order dated 08.08.2013 (Annex.4) is held to be invalid and is set aside.
The respondents are directed to offer appointment to the petitioner for the post in question.

Since vide an administrative order dated 08.08.2013 (Annex.4), a decision was taken to keep the seat vacant, subject to the outcome of the proceedings pending before competent criminal court, benefit of said vacancy be given to the petitioner.

12. The petitioner be accorded notional benefits along with seniority as given to her counter-parts,
with whom the petitioner had competed in the same selection process, for the period during which the petitioner remained out of service, following the temporary termination order.
13. Needful exercise be carried out within a period of three months from the date of receipt of web-print of this order.
14. Pending application(s), if any, also stand(s) disposed of.

(ARUN MONGA),J 156-AnilKC/-
